code.note: Every result here was produced by committed code. The 2026-07-26 Step 4 receipt also attests committed code by bytes (its recorded source.py/segments.py digests match 414964d exactly) - the first version of this receipt wrongly said otherwise. The divergence below is environmental, not a code change.

decision.basis: Among the three arms the July rule ADMITS, all tie at Recall@50 = 0.8000 and structure-overlap takes the Recall@10 tiebreak 20/35 to 18/35. It is indistinguishable from structure-first under McNemar, Wilcoxon and a paired bootstrap, and the two swap nominal winner by metric; the tiebreak is inertia, not evidence. Note this verdict is conditional on slice-level containment, which excludes semantic-embedding - see semantic_embedding_gold_miss.

execution.note: Zero paid API calls. Boundary-selection calls are the local HeuristicBoundarySelector; the single embedding call is the pinned local BGE provider. The OpenAI arms of the July comparison were deliberately not re-run.

divergence_root_cause.human_decision: Identify the environmental variable, pin it, and re-baseline deliberately. NOT 'accept or revert e0af2b9' - that commit is not the cause and could not be reverted anyway.
divergence_root_cause.leading_hypothesis: source.py::_markup_drafts swallows AssertionError/ValueError from _MarkupBoundaryParser (a stdlib html.parser.HTMLParser subclass) and silently falls back to a coarser drafting strategy. A CPython html.parser change flips that path.
divergence_root_cause.mitigation_applied: Interpreter pinned to 3.12.9 (.python-version, requires-python >=3.12,<3.13). This is a hypothesis under test, not a confirmed remedy: 3.12.9 may already be the new behaviour.
divergence_root_cause.probe: Under CPython 3.12.9 the parser does NOT raise on congress_bills.xml_text for 118-hr-8862 and the markup path yields 3427 drafts; the July run recorded only 174 xml_text slices for that artifact.
divergence_root_cause.why_not_proven: No receipt anywhere records an interpreter version, so July's interpreter cannot be re-run.

paired_magnitude_tests.conclusion: Magnitude-based tests DO reach significance where binarised R@10 could not. structure-overlap and structure-first remain indistinguishable under every test and swap nominal winner by metric (structure-first ahead on RR, structure-overlap ahead on nDCG@10). Under Bonferroni across the eight tests run, only llm-guided - structure-overlap on RR survives at 0.05/8.
paired_magnitude_tests.method: per-query reciprocal rank and nDCG@10; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and 200,000-resample paired bootstrap; corpus scope, 35 queries

paired_significance_recall_at_10.power_note: Among the LOSSLESS arms the largest discordance is 3. Across all five arms it is 7-1 (llm-guided vs paragraph-sentence, p=0.0703). An exact two-sided sign test on 35 queries CAN reach p<0.05 - it needs a 6-0 split or better. What this corpus cannot resolve are effects of the size observed among the lossless arms.
paired_significance_recall_at_10.test: exact two-sided McNemar over 35 paired queries

segment_count_drift_from_july.attribution: NOT a code change. See divergence_root_cause.
segment_count_drift_from_july.scope_note: 'The entire delta is one artifact' holds only for the two structure arms. gao-26-108625 is the only artifact anywhere that GAINED a segment.

semantic_embedding_gold_miss.open_decision: Whether containment should be slice-level or segment-level. Under segment-level containment semantic-embedding contains 35/35 and wins the declared ordering on its FIRST criterion (R@50, 31/35 vs 28/35).
semantic_embedding_gold_miss.verdict: Not a retrieval loss. The span is fully present, verbatim and uncut, inside a single segment. It is marked missed only because _relevant(contain=True) requires one SLICE to enclose it. The three arms that pass do so by emitting one uncut [0,9909) slice - they pass by not slicing at all, not by slicing better.
